knowns.fact: Stance: MIT decided; PR and issue templates wanted (redirect first-principle clashes to 'raise it in your own Ang', plus an open-conversation template); no markdown linting
Full kit (C): ESLint, Prettier, Vitest, Husky, lint-staged and CI, dev-only at the repo root; Zac's call 2026-11-16 because the code will be read and bears his name
knowns.answers: Is quality tooling for the Ang repo worth it: none, B (zero-dep node --check/--test in CI) or C (dev-only full kit)?

knowns.fact: The test command documented in 10k/technical/project-structure.md runs 0 of 37 tests (Node's glob skips .claude/); fixing it is part of this idea's tooling work: use 'src/.claude/**/*.test.mjs' or a package.json test script

Small whimsical repos keep README+LICENSE (+changelog if versioned), put 'fork it' in the README, mostly drop CoC/SECURITY/CONTRIBUTORS, and use issue templates with blank issues off routing chat to Discussions; three candidate kits for shaping
knowns.answers: Which standards do small, whimsical open-source projects keep, and which suit Ang?

decisions.decision: Adopt C: lint to zero errors and zero warnings, with auto-fix on (ESLint --fix and Prettier --write on commit); markdown is ignored by every linter and formatter
Go full grown-up repo: status badges on the README (CI and the like), not a minimal look
Sane defaults: Prettier as shipped plus semicolons and trailing commas, set explicitly; ESLint with the style and syntax plugins the community treats as sane defaults
CONTRIBUTING points people to the issue and PR templates and says how to use them; the README links to it
No account-level zacbraddy/.github defaults (kit 3 out): hygiene files live in the Ang repo only, since not every repo needs this rigour and copy-paste suits the few that do (Zac, 2026-11-16)

Kit 2: kit 1 (README 'fork it' section, issue templates with blank issues off, fork-aware PR template, private vulnerability reporting on) plus a short CONTRIBUTING and a short code of conduct in Ang's voice (Zac's preference, 2026-11-16)
